newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS BEAT CANADIENS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS BEAT CANADIENS.

text.p: Jozef Stumpel's goal with 1:58 left in the third period snapped a tie and gave the Boston Bruins a 5-4 victory over the Montreal Canadiens, who had their seven-game unbeaten streak snapped on Thursday.
Montreal pulled Thibault for an extra attacker with 14 seconds remaining, but was unable to test goaltender Rob Tallas, who finished with 25 saves.
Rick Tocchet scored twice, Sheldon Kennedy had a goal and an assist and Stumpel added a pair of assists for the Bruins, who have won three of their last four games.

In Calgary, Jarome Iginla's wrist shot beat Jean-Sebastian Giguere to the stick side with 5:34 left in regulation as the Calgary Flames extended their winning streak to three games with a 3-2 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Dale McTavish's first NHL goal, midway through the final period, knotted the game for Calgary.
Kevin Dineen and Keith Primeau scorred for Hartford.
In Los Angeles, Dimitri Khristich had two goals and two assists and Ian Laperriere scored 3:25 into the third period to snap a tie as the Los Angeles Kings beat the Buffalo Sabres 6-3.
Kevin Stevens, Philippe Boucher and Jan Vopat also scored and Vladimir Tsyplakov set up three goals for the Kings.
Jason Dawe scored his 10th goal of the season in the third period to lift Buffalo into a 3-3 tie, but Laperriere got his fourth goal just over two minutes later to give the Kings the lead for good.

In Ottawa, Patrick Roy recorded his league-leading sixth shutout and Adam Deadmarsh scored one goal and set up the other as the Colorado Avalanche extended their unbeaten streak to nine games with a 2-0 blanking of the Ottawa Senators.
Roy made 33 saves for his 36th career shutout, tops among active goaltenders.
Deadmarsh has 11 goals and 18 points in his last 16 games.
In Philadelphia, The Philadelphia Flyers had their 17-game unbeaten streak snapped as Patrick Poulin scored twice and Corey Schwab made 30 saves in a 3-1 victory by the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Philadelphia suffered its first loss since a 4-1 defeat to the New York Islanders on November 27th. The Flyers had been 14-0-3 since then.
Dino Ciccarelli's goal with 6:58 to go in the third period broke a tie and put the Lightning ahead to stay.
In Phoenix, Igor Larionov scored 58 seconds into overtime to give the Detroit Red Wings a 5-4 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes, snapping their season-high four-game winless streak.
Shanahan had two goals and an assist for the Red Wings, who had been 0-3-1 in their previous four games.
"We should've won tonight, sometimes you don't win games you should, but tonight we did," Detroit coach Scotty Bowman said.

In San Jose, Pierre Turgeon scored a power-play goal off a rebound with 25.4 seconds left in the third period to give the St. Louis Blues their first win under coach Joel Quenneville, a 4-3 triumph over the San Jose Sharks.

Referee Paul Devorski penalised Sharks defenceman Jeff Bodger for high-sticking with 1:04 to go and the Blues cashed in with their first power-play goal in three games. It was Turgeon's seventh goal of the season and second in three games.

In Washington, Olaf Kolzig continued his torrid play with his second shutout in six days and Peter Bondra scored his ninth goal in eight games as the Washington Capitals blanked the New York Rangers, 2-0.
Kolzig turned aside 25 shots, and in his last three starts, he has alowed one goal while stopping 71 shots.
